compressed.text: I'm just gonna talk for a few minutes about a few different topics so that I have something to test my video editor on.
The first thing I want to talk about is how the transcription step works.

Basically, the system takes a raw video file, runs it through a speech-to-text model called Whisper, and gets back a time-stamped transcript so every sentence has an exact start and end time in the original video.
The way it works is you take the video and it listens to it and figures out what words are being said and it knows what time each word happens.
Actually, random side note, I had coffee this morning and it was way too strong.

Anyway, the second part is a segment selection, and LLM reads through all of the transcript segments along with a brief, only keep the technical parts, and decides which ones to keep and which to cut.
Kind of like how a human editor would skim through and mark things up.
And the last piece, the one I'm most excited about, is that the system can actually splice the footage back together automatically using FMPEG.
So you end up with a fully edited video without ever opening a timeline editor by hand.
That's the three parts, transcription, and then the selection thing, and then the last one with the video stuff.
I think that's everything I wanted to cover.
